guides.title: Pension life certificate from home: Jeevan Pramaan face scan in 4 steps
guides.summary: Pensioners can give their yearly life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) from an Android phone with a face scan, without going to the bank. The 2026 campaign runs from 1 to 30 November. A family member can do it on their own phone with the pensioner present.

steps.title: Install two apps from Google Play
steps.body: On an Android phone, open Google Play and install Jeevan Pramaan (the face authentication app) and AadhaarFaceRD (UIDAI's face capture service). AadhaarFaceRD has no icon on the home screen; that is normal, it runs in the background (you can see it under Settings, Apps). The official manual asks for Android 9 or newer, a 5 MP or better camera and an internet connection.

steps.title: Register the operator once
steps.body: Open Jeevan Pramaan. On Device Registration and Operator Identification, the person running the phone (a son, daughter, or the pensioner) enters their Aadhaar number, mobile number and email, enters the OTP, adds their name, ticks consent and taps Scan. Keep the face inside the circle and blink when asked. This is a one-time step per phone.

steps.title: Enter the pensioner's details
steps.body: On Pensioner Identification, enter the pensioner's Aadhaar number and mobile number and the OTP sent to that mobile. Then fill or check the PPO number, pension account number, bank details, Pension Sanctioning Authority and Pension Disbursing Authority. Check the preview carefully (wrong details lead to rejection), tick both boxes and tap Submit.

steps.title: Scan the pensioner's face and save the Pramaan ID
steps.body: Tick consent and tap Scan. The pensioner looks straight at the camera in good, even light, with eyes open, a neutral face and clear glasses only. On success the screen shows a Pramaan ID and an SMS with the ID and a download link arrives. Later, download the certificate at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to check whether the pension office accepted it.

guides.tip: Do it well before 30 November. Pensioners aged 80 and above could submit from 1 October. If the app does not work for you, the bank branch, post office (India Post Payments Bank) or a Common Service Centre can do it.
guides.caution: No bank or government office asks for an OTP or PIN on a phone call. If someone calls saying the pension will stop unless you share an OTP, it is fraud: hang up and call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in. Install apps only from Google Play. Screen labels can change slightly with app versions; follow the official manual.

guides.title: Reel music muted (Audio unavailable)? 3 rules to keep your sound
guides.summary: If your reel says Audio unavailable, a copyright system usually removed the song. Three habits keep your music safe: add songs inside Instagram, use the right account type, and use royalty-free music for promotions. We also show how we make our own background music.

steps.title: Add the song inside Instagram
steps.body: In the Reels editor, tap the music (audio) option and pick a song from Instagram's own library. Songs mixed into the video in another editing app, or downloaded from YouTube or Spotify, are a common reason reels get muted.

steps.title: Check your account type
steps.body: Business accounts get only commercially licensed audio, a much smaller library. If you are a creator, not a shop: open your profile, tap the menu (three lines), then Account type and tools (on some versions Business tools and controls), then Switch account type, then Switch to creator account. Menu labels can differ slightly by app version.

steps.title: Use royalty-free music for promos
steps.body: For a shop, brand or paid promotion, do not use popular film songs. Business accounts see Meta's royalty-free Sound Collection in the same music picker; it is cleared for Facebook and Instagram only. For YouTube videos, use YouTube Studio, then Audio library, and filter by Attribution not required (Creative Commons tracks need a credit in the description).

steps.title: Or make your own music
steps.body: We make the background music for our reels ourselves with a small script that synthesises lo-fi chords and a beat (engine/lofi.py in our public repo github.com/veereshkumbar/technibaba-reels). Music you create yourself has no other rights owner.

guides.tip: If a reel is already muted, edit it with a song from Instagram's library or repost it with cleared audio. If you think the mute was a mistake, you can appeal in the app.
guides.caution: Even songs from Instagram's library can be muted later if the rights change. Do not switch a business account just to use popular songs in ads or brand posts: commercial use needs licensed music. This is general platform guidance, not legal advice.

guides.title: How to check which SIM cards are issued in your name (Sanchar Saathi)
guides.summary: Someone can get a SIM card using your ID without you knowing. The government's Sanchar Saathi website shows every mobile number registered in your name, and lets you report the ones that are not yours. It takes about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Open the official Sanchar Saathi website
steps.body: Type sancharsaathi.gov.in in your browser yourself (do not use links from messages). Go to Citizen Centric Services, then choose Know Mobile Connections in Your Name. The same option is in the Sanchar Saathi app.

steps.title: Log in with your mobile number and OTP
steps.body: Enter your 10-digit mobile number and the captcha (if shown), then enter the OTP sent to that number. Use a number that is active and in your own name.

steps.title: Check the list of numbers
steps.body: The page shows every mobile number registered against your identity, across all operators. Go through it slowly. Most people can have at most 9 connections in their name (6 in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam and the North-Eastern states).

steps.title: Report what is not yours, or not needed
steps.body: For a number you never took, select Not My Number. For an old number of yours that you no longer use, select Not Required. Then press Report. You get a ticket or reference number; the operator verifies the request and disconnects the number. Check again after a few weeks.

guides.tip: Do the same check for your parents and grandparents, using their phone for the OTP. Older family members are often the ones whose documents get misused.
guides.caution: Sanchar Saathi never asks for your bank details, card number or UPI PIN. If a SIM in your name was used for fraud, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. Screen labels can change slightly; follow the wording on the official site.

guides.title: The first 3 seconds: our reel hook formula (with our own numbers)
guides.summary: On one of our reels 75% of viewers skipped in the first 3 seconds; on another only 26% did. Three things were different. These are our own Insights numbers, not a guarantee.

steps.title: Show the result in frame 0
steps.body: The first frame is also the thumbnail. Put the payoff there (a number, a result, a before/after) with a 3-5 word headline. Do not open with a logo, an intro or a greeting.

steps.title: Ask a question or make a claim within 1.5 seconds
steps.body: The first line should land within 1.5 seconds: a question, a disagreement or a surprising number. Put the same words on screen, because many people watch reels muted.

steps.title: Keep it short: 35-45 seconds
steps.body: On our 60-second test reels, viewers stayed for only 7-12 seconds. We now make 35-45 second reels and deliver the payoff before the 80% mark.

steps.title: Check your own numbers
steps.body: In each reel's Insights, look at the skip rate (how many people swiped away in the first 3 seconds) and the average watch time, and compare every new reel with the previous one. End with a prompt to send the reel to a friend: according to Instagram head Adam Mosseri, the top three ranking signals are watch time, likes and sends.

guides.tip: One reel, one idea. Whatever you want to show goes in the first frame.
guides.caution: These numbers come from our small channel (November 2026). Every channel is different; there is no guarantee of views or followers.

guides.title: Real or fake Wi-Fi? Three checks before you connect
guides.summary: At an airport, cafe or station, if you see two Wi-Fi networks with the same name, run these three checks before you connect.

steps.title: Match the name exactly
steps.body: Ask staff for the exact network name, or check the official sign, ticket or receipt. If even one character differs (for example a zero instead of the letter O in Airport), it is fake. If two networks have the same name, confirm with staff before connecting.

steps.title: Look at what the login page asks for
steps.body: Genuine public Wi-Fi usually asks only for a mobile number and OTP, or a room or ticket number. If the page asks for a bank password, card number, UPI PIN or email password, close it immediately. It is a fake page.

steps.title: Take browser warnings seriously
steps.body: If the browser shows 'Your connection is not private' or 'Not secure', tap 'Go back'. Never tap 'Proceed'.

steps.title: If you already connected
steps.body: Open your phone's Wi-Fi settings, tap the network and choose 'Forget this network'. Change any password you entered right away and turn on two-step verification for that account.

guides.tip: Outside home, do banking and payments only on mobile data. Use free Wi-Fi only for browsing.
guides.caution: This is a general safety guide. If you lose money, call your bank immediately and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on the 1930 helpline (India).

guides.title: Free airport Wi-Fi can be a trap
guides.summary: An open Wi-Fi network without a password can be a fake hotspot set up to steal passwords. Here is the simple rule that keeps you safe.

steps.title: Understand the risk
steps.body: Anyone can create a hotspot with an official-sounding name (for example Free_Airport_WiFi_Fast). Once you connect, it can show a fake login page and capture your password.

steps.title: Bank only on mobile data
steps.body: In public places, use your own mobile data for UPI, net banking and online payments.

steps.title: Turn off auto-join
steps.body: In your phone's Wi-Fi settings, turn off auto-join for open networks so the phone does not connect to a fake network on its own.

steps.title: Learn to spot the real network
steps.body: See our guide on the three checks: the network name, the login page and browser warnings.

guides.tip: Free Wi-Fi is for browsing. Money goes over mobile data.
guides.caution: This is a general safety guide. If you are defrauded, call your bank immediately and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on the 1930 helpline (India).
